title: SpaceX and Tesla Put the Cost of AI in Focus
gist: SpaceX (Tuesday) and Tesla (Wednesday) earnings will test whether Musk's core businesses can fund escalating AI spending amid merger speculation. SpaceX spent $15.8 billion on AI capex last quarter and Tesla's free cash flow is expected to be deeply negative.

insights.claim: SpaceX and Tesla earnings this week will test whether Musk's established businesses can support increasingly expensive AI ambitions, with SpaceX reporting Tuesday and Tesla Wednesday.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Earnings are a read-through on how long AI capex can be financed internally.
insights.locator: SpaceX and Tesla’s earnings this week

insights.claim: SpaceX spent $15.8 billion on AI capital investment in the previous quarter, and analysts expect quarterly revenue of about $12.74 billion.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: AI capex exceeding quarterly revenue shows the scale of commitment relative to the base business.
insights.quote: The company spent $15.8 billion on AI capital investment in the previous quarter

insights.claim: Analysts forecast Tesla revenue of about $27.88 billion and adjusted EPS of 43 cents versus 50 cents a year earlier, with heavy spending expected to push quarterly free cash flow deeply negative despite stronger deliveries.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Vehicle profits are not covering robotaxi, humanoid robot and AI infrastructure spending.

insights.claim: Speculation is building about a SpaceX-Tesla merger that neither company nor Musk has formally endorsed, and a deal would raise valuation, ownership, voting control and risk-allocation questions for shareholders.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Shared leadership does not guarantee a combination benefits both shareholder groups equally.
insights.quote: Shared leadership does not automatically mean a transaction benefits both groups equally.
insights.locator: A merger would also raise questions

insights.claim: The most revealing signals will be management's spending commitments and explanations of when investments will produce cash, since revenue growth alone cannot establish sustainable economics.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Watch capex guidance and payback timelines rather than headline revenue.
